class.name: DeltaReplicator
class.brief_description: Replicates properties of a node by sending only what changed, down to array elements and dictionary keys, acknowledged per peer.
class.description: For large or structured state - lists, dictionaries, reports. A property synchronizer sends every value whole on every update, and all of a node's values have to fit into one packet; this sends nothing while nothing changes, and a change costs about the size of the change. Every [member check_interval] the server compares each property with its last recorded state - deeply, so arrays and dictionaries edited in place are noticed - and records a new numbered state when something differs. Each client is sent the patch from the state it confirmed last to the newest one. With [constant DELIVERY_ACKNOWLEDGED] the patch goes unreliably and the client acknowledges every state it applies; until it does, the server re-sends every [member resend_interval] - the patch from the confirmed state to whatever is newest then, never the lost packet itself - so a client that missed something catches up in one step and a slow link never queues stale data. With [constant DELIVERY_RELIABLE] patches go over a reliable, ordered RPC, each from the previous state. A client asks for the full values when its replicator is ready (sent reliably), so a peer joining late starts from the current state. [member keyed_arrays] matches the Dictionary elements of an Array by a key field instead of by index: removing one from the middle sends its key, a moved one sends the key order, and clients get [signal element_added], [signal element_removed] and [signal element_changed]. [PlayerState], [GameStateBase] and [Pawn] replicate through one (a child named [code]Replication[/code], checked every physics frame, with their own C++ properties push-based) for the names returned by [code]_get_replicated_properties()[/code] and [code]_get_delta_replicated_properties()[/code] ([code]"orders:id"[/code] keys an array); it can also be placed on any node. Patch format, as returned by [method make_patch]: [code]{"=": value}[/code] - the whole value; [code]{"a": size, "i": {index: patch}}[/code] - an [Array]'s new size and changed elements; [code]{"k": field, "u": {key: patch}, "r": [keys], "o": [keys]}[/code] - a keyed [Array]'s changed and added elements, removed keys and, when something moved, the key order; [code]{"d": {key: patch}, "-": [keys]}[/code] - a [Dictionary]'s changed and removed keys. Packed arrays, differently typed containers, and any value whose patch would not be smaller go whole.

method.name: apply_patch
method.description: [param old_value] with the patch applied. Containers are copied, never changed in place; a typed Array stays typed.

method.name: client_receive_full_state
method.description: RPC: the full values of state [param seq].

method.name: client_receive_patch
method.description: RPC: patches by property name, turning state [param base] into state [param seq].

method.name: client_receive_patch_reliable
method.description: RPC: [method client_receive_patch] for a patch too big to go unreliably.

method.name: flush
method.description: Server: compares now and sends whatever changed, without waiting for the next check - e.g. before a change carried by another synchronizer that must not arrive first. Returns [code]true[/code] when there was a change.

method.name: get_bytes_sent
method.description: Server: encoded bytes sent so far, full states and patches, summed over receiving peers.

method.name: get_comparisons_skipped
method.description: Server: how many times a push-based property was left uncompared because nothing marked it.

method.name: get_patches_sent
method.description: Server: how many patches have been sent, re-sends included.

method.name: get_peer_acked_sequence
method.description: Server: the newest state [param peer] confirmed, or [code]-1[/code].

method.name: get_reliable_patches
method.description: Server: patches sent reliably for being over [member max_unreliable_bytes].

method.name: get_resends
method.description: Server: how many sends repeated a state the peer had already been sent, for want of an acknowledgement.

method.name: get_state_sequence
method.description: The newest state number: on the server the latest recorded, on a client the latest applied.

method.name: has_full_state
method.description: On a client: whether the full values have arrived (patches are ignored before that).

method.name: make_patch
method.description: The patch turning [param old_value] into [param new_value], or [code]null[/code] when they are equal. With [param key_field], an Array of Dictionaries is matched by that field.

method.name: mark_element_dirty
method.description: Server: in a push-based keyed array, the element with [param key] changed, was added or was removed. Only marked elements are looked at; the others are taken from the previous state without being compared or copied. On a property that is not a keyed array this marks the whole property.

method.name: mark_property_dirty
method.description: Server: a push-based property changed - it is compared whole at the next check. Harmless on a polled property.

method.name: server_ack
method.description: RPC: a client confirms it applied state [param seq].

method.name: server_request_full_state
method.description: RPC: a client asks for the full values and starts receiving patches.

members.member: Seconds between comparisons on the server. [code]0[/code] checks every physics frame.
Property name to key field: that Array's Dictionary elements are matched by the field. Elements that are not Dictionaries, lack the field or share a key fall back to matching by index.
How many states the server keeps to build patches from. A peer further behind gets the full values.
With [constant DELIVERY_ACKNOWLEDGED]: a patch bigger than this is sent reliably instead - an unreliable packet over the MTU is split, and losing any piece loses it.
Names of the properties to replicate.

Properties compared only when marked with [method mark_property_dirty] or [method mark_element_dirty] - push-based. In debug builds every [member push_validation_interval] they are compared anyway, and a change nobody marked is reported and replicated.
Debug builds: seconds between full comparisons of the push-based properties, to catch changes that were not marked. [code]0[/code] turns it off.
With [constant DELIVERY_ACKNOWLEDGED]: how long the server waits for an acknowledgement before sending the newest patch again.
The node whose properties are replicated, relative to this one.

signal.name: element_added
signal.description: On a client: a keyed array gained an element.

signal.name: element_changed
signal.description: On a client: an element of a keyed array changed.

signal.name: element_removed
signal.description: On a client: a keyed array lost an element.

signal.name: property_changed
signal.description: On a client: a property was set from the full state or a patch.

signal.name: synchronized
signal.description: On a client: a full state or a patch was applied.

constants.constant: Every peer that has the node.
Only the peer owning the replicated node.
Unreliable patches, acknowledged per peer, re-sent from the confirmed state until the newest is confirmed.
Reliable, ordered patches, each from the previous state.
